title: Neural Collapse Anchored Prompt Tuning for Generalizable Vision-Language Models

problem.claim: The mechanisms behind learned text representations in vision-language models are unknown, limiting further generalization, with greater limitations under class imbalance in web-sourced datasets.

gap.claim: Neural collapse has been studied in vision-only models, but its role in vision-language model representations had not been examined through prompt tuning.

contributions.claim: Neural-collapse optimality of text-to-image representations is positively correlated with downstream generalizability, with the relationship more pronounced under class imbalance.
Neural-collapse-anchored Prompt Tuning learns prompts whose text and image representations satisfy the same simplex Equiangular Tight Frame.
The method uses language-modality collapse and multi-modality isomorphism regularization and is compatible with other prompt tuning methods.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe this as the first attempt to use neural collapse to examine representations in vision-language models via prompt tuning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments report that the proposed method consistently improves existing prompt tuning techniques across 11 datasets in balanced and imbalanced settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Prompt tuning enables strong downstream generalization for large-scale vision-language models.
Unknown text-representation mechanisms limit further gains, especially under class imbalance.
Neural collapse and the simplex ETF provide a representation-structure lens for studying vision-language models.
The paper examines neural collapse through prompt tuning and proposes neural-collapse-anchored prompt tuning with ETF-aligned representations and two regularizers.
Experiments report consistent improvements across 11 balanced and imbalanced datasets.

source_observation.claim: The paper reports a positive correlation between neural-collapse optimality and downstream generalizability, especially under class imbalance.

interpretation.claim: Representation geometry may be a useful diagnostic or optimization target for improving prompt-tuned model generalization.

application.claim: For vision-language prompt tuning, evaluate and potentially regularize text-image representations toward a shared structured geometry.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported relationship or method generalizes beyond the stated datasets, tasks, or class-imbalance settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the 11 datasets, downstream tasks, baselines, metrics, or improvement magnitudes.
The abstract does not provide theoretical guarantees, ablation results, computational costs, or implementation details.
